name: pnpm
summary: Content-addressed package manager that hard-links a global store instead of copying.
what_it_is: A package manager storing every package version once in a global content-addressed store and hard-linking it into each project, with a strict node_modules layout that prevents access to undeclared dependencies.
why_it_matters: The disk and speed win is the headline, but the strictness matters more: pnpm will not let you import a package you did not declare, which catches a class of bug that npm silently permits and that only surfaces later when a transitive dependency changes. Its workspace support is the usual reason monorepos adopt it.
suitable_for: Teams wanting undeclared-dependency errors caught at install time
not_suitable_for: Projects depending on packages that rely on a flat, permissive node_modules layout
Environments where the hard-link store causes trouble, such as some Docker layer setups
verifiable_facts: Official docs describe a content-addressed store, hard-linking, and a strict non-flat node_modules layout.
editorial_interpretation: That strictness matters more than the disk saving.
